application_scope.IF: Immunofluorescence results are fixation and permeabilisation dependent.

scope: Results are based on consensus protocols. Antibody performance is protocol and sample dependent, and these results do not validate or invalidate experiments in other assay systems or sample types.
scope_short: Result from consensus protocols. Antibody performance is protocol and sample dependent.

ab51243.statement: This antibody (ab51243) is specific to the p16 ARC protein […] There is no observed cross reactivity to the CDKN2A/p16INK4a protein.

beta-galactosidase.short: This is an antibody to the Escherichia coli LacZ beta-galactosidase used in reporter systems. It is not an antibody to the mammalian GLB1 enzyme behind senescence-associated beta-galactosidase. The two share a name and a substrate, and about 20% sequence identity — no better than chance.
beta-galactosidase.source: Do bacteria grow old as we do? — Sholto David, For Better Science, 21 July 2026

p-erk-for-perk.short: This is an antibody to phosphorylated ERK1/2, the growth-signalling kinases written p-ERK or pERK. It is not an antibody to PERK (EIF2AK3), the endoplasmic reticulum kinase of the unfolded protein response. The confusion runs both ways, and this is the rarer direction.
p-erk-for-perk.source: PERK vs p-ERK: Another Antibody Confusion! — Sholto David, Sholto's Substack, 25 August 2026

p16-ink4a.short: This is an antibody to ARPC5, also called p16-ARC — a subunit of the actin-related protein 2/3 complex. It is not an antibody to p16-INK4a, the CDKN2A tumour suppressor and senescence marker usually meant by "p16". The two proteins share a name and a molecular weight and nothing else.
p16-ink4a.source: Mind over Antibody — Sholto David, For Better Science, 2 June 2026

perk-for-p-erk.short: This is an antibody to PERK (EIF2AK3), the endoplasmic reticulum kinase that coordinates the unfolded protein response. It is not an antibody to phosphorylated ERK1/2, the growth-signalling kinases written p-ERK or pERK. The two are unrelated proteins whose abbreviations differ by a hyphen, and they run at different sizes: PERK at about 125 kDa, ERK1/2 as the familiar double band near 42 and 44 kDa.
perk-for-p-erk.source: PERK vs p-ERK: Another Antibody Confusion! — Sholto David, Sholto's Substack, 25 August 2026
